overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Board owed no pre-meeting access, the chair could mute a remote attendee who had non-verbal recording options, and other claims were withdrawn or declined. Only a non-binding encouragement was given.

allegations.summary: Complainant, attending remotely as a disability accommodation, alleged the Board did not provide the audio feed before the meeting began.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law requires public access to meetings, not to the moments before the meeting when members are waiting for the meeting to begin, nor the moments after the meeting when members are gathering their things and filing out of the meeting room.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the chair improperly muted his microphone for the whole meeting, preventing him from telling the Board he wished to record it.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it muted the complainant through the entire meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to announce that the meeting was being recorded.
Complainant alleged Board members debated his remote access and Teams use with staff before the meeting was called to order.
allegations.key_passage: there is no evidence that the brief exchange between or among the Board and IT staff, which occurred prior to the meeting and which is seen but not heard on the recording, constituted deliberation outside of a meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged he missed the start of the meeting because he did not hear a call to order.
allegations.key_passage: To the extent that the complainant alleges that he must have missed the beginning of the meeting because he did not hear a call of the meeting to order, we deny review of this allegation.
